item.title: Libya’s NOC eyes 2 million oil bpd production in 3 years, acting chairman says
item.description: ‎The Acting Chairman of the National Oil Corporation (NOC), Masoud Suleiman, has said that the NOC is determined to reach a production of two million barrels per day (bpd) within the next three years provided that sufficient funding would be provided to achieve this goal. item.title: Libya’s NOC to halt oil-for-fuel trade next March
item.description: The Acting Chairman of the National Oil Corporation (NOC), Masoud Suleiman, indicated that the payment mechanism for the partners of Al-Waha and Eni for gas supplies will be stopped, and the exchange of crude oil for fuel will also be halted on the first of next March. item.title: Central Bank of Libya issues new banknotes’ print
item.description: The Central Bank of Libya (CBL) has announced issuing new banknotes in denominations of [5, 10, and 20] dinars. The CBL has explained that the 10 dinars denomination will be issued next week, followed by the other denominations, adding that they all will bear the signature of the new Governor Naji Issa. item.title: Promising future for Libya’s oil production
item.description: Libya is actively pursuing a significant increase in its oil production over the next three years, aiming to reach 2 million barrels per day (bpd) – according to the newly-appointed head of the National Oil Corporation (NOC). As of January 2025, Libya’s output stands at approximately 1.41 million bpd. item.title: Human rights groups call for investigating torture crimes at Garnada prison
item.description: The World Organization Against Torture (OMCT) and the Libyan Anti-Torture Network (LAN) have denounced the systematic and widespread torture documented at Garnada prison in eastern Libya. saying that despite years of calls for accountability for military and security forces implicated in severe human rights violations, the abuses persist, prompting urgent demands for action. item.title: The Maltese Herald: Haftar has sent military trucks to Sudan’s RSF
item.description: The Maltese Herald newspaper reported that Khalifa Haftar had sent military trucks to Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in preparation for a major battle in Al Fashir. item.title: Dbeibah: Libya retrieves 15 billion euros after Belgian court ruling

item.title: Hanna Tetteh of Ghana appointed 9th UN envoy to Libya
